teach.heading: Stocks are about ownership. Futures are about movement.
teach.body: That is the cleanest way to separate them. With stocks, you are buying ownership in a company. With futures, you are trading a contract based on price movement. That difference changes how you think about direction, risk, flexibility, and why the Dayli ICC method makes more sense in futures.
teach.dayliNote: Futures naturally fit long and short thinking — that flexibility is exactly why this training is built around futures, not stocks.

experience.prompt: Which statement sounds like futures thinking: "I want to own this for 10 years" or "I think price is about to move"?

reinforce.question: A trader wants to profit from a short-term price move without caring at all about long-term company ownership. Which instrument type is built for that goal, and why?
options: Futures — a futures contract is based purely on price movement, not ownership
Stocks — stock ownership was always designed for short-term moves
Neither — instrument choice has nothing to do with that goal
